inside.description: The source is spatially contained within the target Region.

near.description: The source should be spatially close to the target. Exact distance is backend-defined.

far_from.description: The source should maintain clear spatial separation from the target. Exact distance is backend-defined.

along.description: The source is placed or distributed along the target Network.

direction_of.description: The source lies in the specified qualitative direction relative to the target.

Placement.description: Backend-independent spatial placement semantics. anchor is world-relative; relations are object-relative and conjunctive.

Topology.description: Network connectivity/topology, intentionally separate from spatial placement.

Amount.description: One authoritative way to describe global population amount: exact count or qualitative density.

Arrangement.description: How instances are arranged within their placement domain. uniform means approximately even spacing, random means irregular stochastic placement without strong grouping, clustered means local groups separated by sparser space.

SpatialSelector.description: A qualitative spatial locus used by density profiles. This is not an object placement relation; it selects where on a profile an endpoint applies.

DensityProfile.description: How qualitative density varies across space. V2 currently supports a continuous qualitative gradient between two spatial selectors; exact interpolation is backend-defined.

Population.description: Population semantics for repeated objects. arrangement is orthogonal to density specification. amount.mode=count may coexist with density_profile as a total budget; amount.mode=density is a uniform/global density specification and is mutually exclusive with density_profile.

constraints.message: population.amount.mode=density and population.density_profile are mutually exclusive: qualitative density is a uniform/global density specification, while density_profile is a spatially varying density specification. Use one or the other.

semantic_notes: World IR V2 separates orthogonal semantic axes instead of adding many primitive-specific flat fields.
placement answers WHERE: world-relative anchor and object-relative relations. A placement may use either or both, and relations are conjunctive.
topology answers HOW A NETWORK CONNECTS: Network from/to/via live only inside topology and are separate from placement.

population answers HOW A REPEATED SET IS REALIZED. arrangement is orthogonal to density specification; count may serve as a total budget, while qualitative amount density and density_profile are alternative density specifications.
population.amount uses exactly one mode: count for an exact/non-negative target count, or density for qualitative uniform/global density.
population.arrangement describes instance-to-instance arrangement inside the placement domain. It does not decide where the distribution is located.

uniform means approximately even spacing, not necessarily a literal grid. random means irregular stochastic placement without strong clustering. clustered means local groups separated by relatively sparse space.
population.density_profile describes spatial variation of density and is orthogonal to arrangement. A distribution may therefore be clustered while also becoming denser along a gradient.
The gradient profile is qualitative and continuous in semantic intent. Exact interpolation, thresholds, coordinates, and sampling algorithms are backend-defined.

A gradient SpatialSelector identifies a qualitative locus within the Distribution placement domain. selector anchor=west means the world-west side of that domain; direction_of(target=forest, west) instead means a locus west of the forest and must not be used as shorthand for the forest interior west side.

If density_profile is present, amount.mode=count may still provide a total instance budget. amount.mode=density is mutually exclusive with density_profile. When an edit changes a uniform/global qualitative density into a spatial gradient, replacing amount.mode=density with density_profile is the requested density change and is not a preservation violation.
inside, near, far_from, along, and direction_of are shared placement relations rather than primitive-specific fields.
near and far_from remain qualitative. Numeric distance/spacing is intentionally outside V2 until a real use case requires it.
Do not encode stylistic labels such as natural, eerie, civilized, or wild directly in the IR when they can be semantically lowered into placement/population structure.
Do not invent fields, relation types, arrangement types, profile types, selector types, or enum values absent from this specification.
If a user intent still cannot be represented without losing an essential semantic constraint, return an IR capability gap rather than silently approximating it.

migration_from_v1.relations: Move to placement.relations without changing relation objects.
migration_from_v1.count_and_density_together: V2 amount has one authoritative mode. If a V1 Distribution contains both count and density, resolve the intended authority explicitly rather than migrating both automatically.
migration_from_v1.new_arrangement: Use population.arrangement only when the user/world state specifies an arrangement semantic. Omitted does not mean uniform.
migration_from_v1.new_density_profile: Use population.density_profile for explicit spatial density variation such as a continuous low-to-high gradient.
